ESOL / English for Non-native Speakers (Part-time)
These programmes improve skills in English speaking, reading and writing to help non-native speakers to better integrate into the society in which they live and may work. ESOL and FENNS (Functional English for Non-Native Speakers) classes are for adult learners who have the right to be resident in the UK.
This part-time programme runs from September to July and will focus on developing all English language skills at the relevant level. We will help you to assess the right level for your current ability.
Pre-entry (Beginners) A foundation class aimed at speakers with very little or no English. By the end of the first year you will be able to use basic English, and have a simple conversation at home, in the workplace and in the community.
Entry Level 1, 2, 3 (Improvers) Improves skills in English speaking, reading and writing to help you to better integrate into the society in which you live and may work.
Level 1 (Intermediate) Develop more complex English language skills in reading, writing, speaking and listening. Explore new grammar and concepts that improve your confidence and help you to progress towards further learning or skilled employment.
Level 2 (Advanced) Designed to develop and enhance your English language skills to a similar level to GCSE (at grade 4). It will enable you to use language to participate effectively in society and employment.
You will be required to undertake a diagnostic assessment prior to acceptance on the programme.
Each level has entry requirements. We will help you to assess the right level for your current ability.
Edexcel Functional Skills Qualification in English
Upon successful completion of each year, you will have the opportunity to progress to the next level. Some students who have completed Level 2 may progress to GCSE English, other courses at college, employment or further training.
Written, speaking and listening assessments will take place in class on a regular basis. Controlled assessments (exams) will take place when the teacher feels that you are ready.
You will be expected to practise your English skills outside of class times and will be set one to two hours of homework per week.
This programme does not require you to undertake work experience.
Classes are free for students who have lived in the UK for three years, have taken up permanent residence in the UK, are refugees, are spouses of British Citizens or are under 19. You are required to provide proof of identity at the interview stage (passports, Home Office documents, Identity cards, pre-settled or settled status).
You will need to purchase a textbook each year to support your learning, this cost will be advised at the start of the programme. You will also need to pay a £15 contribution to the student association.
If you do not meet these entry requirements, you may join these classes but there will be an overseas charge.

Mathematics (Part-time)
Mathematics programmes are designed to further improve and enhance personal skills in understanding mathematical methods and concepts. These qualifications are for anyone who has not yet achieved GCSE Mathematics at grade 4 (C).
We will help you to assess the right pathway for your current level. Pathways include:
Brush Up Your Maths (Functional Skills) This will help you build on your practical maths skills to get the most out of work and everyday life. If you need to improve your confidence in your maths then this is the pathway for you.
Key areas of study include: -Using numbers in everyday life
GCSE Mathematics Essential for many higher education courses and careers, GCSE Mathematics will help you to develop knowledge, skills and understanding of mathematical methods and concepts enabling you to better use maths in everyday and real world situations. You will gain confidence in problem solving strategies, logical thinking and handling data, as well as building confidence and skills to solve practical mathematical problems.
Key areas of study include:
You will be required to undertake a diagnostic assessment prior to acceptance on the programme.
Those wishing to take the GCSE pathway should be able to demonstrate a good knowledge of addition, subtraction, multiplication and division skills. You should also be confident in reading and interpreting data and approaching mathematical problems.
These qualifications can support your application to a vocational qualification or support employment applications. GCSE Maths at grade 4 (grade C) is required for entry to Higher and some Further Education courses.
Practice exams and regular progress checks are carried out during the course with one or more external examination papers at the end of the programme.
The final assessment for the GCSE pathway will be three exams. Each exam is 1 hour 30 minutes, and counts for one third of the final grade. Results will be given on a grade system from 1 to 9 (9 being the highest). Our aim is for you to achieve a minimum grade 4 at the end of the programme.
One or two hours of homework will be set each week.
This programme does not require you to undertake work experience.
Programmes are free for qualifying UK and EU/EEA citizen. There are no additional fees associated with this programme.

Skills Partners shape curriculum for Generation Alpha
Generation Alpha is now beginning to enter the workforce with a set of experiences unlike any that came before. Shaped by smartphones, social media, artificial intelligence and the disruption of a global pandemic, these young people are bringing fresh expectations around communication, flexibility and purpose at work. For employers and educators alike, that presents both a challenge and an opportunity: how to recognise the strengths this generation offers, while helping them develop the skills, knowledge and behaviours needed to thrive in the modern workplace.
With those questions in mind, Newbury College brought together local employers and College staff for a Skills Partners Workshop on 15 April 2026. The event provided an opportunity to examine current and future workforce needs, identify priority skills gaps and discuss how education and training can better support businesses, students, apprentices and employees. Representatives from PR Motors, Ortho Surgical Skills Centre, Education Business Partnership, Penny Post, the University of Oxford, Prior's Court, The Vineyard, Environmental Solutions Waste Management and Dovetail and Slate took part in the discussion.
After a welcome from Principal Lee Probert, Deputy Principal Lee Jamieson led the workshop with a presentation on Generation Alpha and the ways this emerging workforce is already beginning to challenge traditional assumptions about learning and work. The presentation described a cohort that has grown up with digital platforms as a normal part of everyday life. It also highlighted formative influences including COVID-19, climate change awareness and digital-first communication, all of which are expected to shape the attitudes and expectations of young people entering employment in the late 2020s.
The session made clear that this is not simply a story about young people being more comfortable with technology. It is about a wider shift in behaviour, suggesting that Generation Alpha is likely to see AI as an everyday tool rather than a specialist one, and may move workplace tasks away from creating from scratch towards curating, checking and improving outputs. It also pointed to a preference for instant and visual communication, regular feedback, flexible working and a stronger focus on outcomes than on hours spent at a desk. Lee’s research highlighted that nearly 80 per cent expect flexibility to be standard and that more than 75 per cent want to be their own boss or build a side hustle.
Those ideas were then tested against the experience of local employers. Working in groups, delegates were asked to identify and rank the skills, knowledge and behaviours they most value in their industries using a diamond ranking exercise. The results were strikingly consistent. Communication appeared repeatedly. So did critical thinking, problem solving, adaptability, resilience, teamwork, independence and accountability.
That consistency matters. It shows that while businesses recognise the growing importance of digital fluency, their priorities remain firmly rooted in the human qualities that help people succeed at work. Employers want people who can think clearly, communicate well, work with others, adapt to change and respond positively to feedback. They also want people who can take responsibility, show motivation and continue learning. In other words, technical confidence matters, but it is not enough on its own.
The workshop painted a balanced picture of the opportunity ahead. Generation Alpha is likely to bring strengths that businesses can benefit from. These include confidence with digital tools, ease in blended physical and digital environments, and a willingness to question established ways of doing things. They may help employers think differently about communication, workflow and the practical use of AI. At the same time, the workshop also underlined the need to help young people develop the habits and behaviours that allow those strengths to translate into long-term success, including resilience, professionalism, sound judgement and the ability to act on feedback.
For Newbury College, this is exactly where partnership with employers is most valuable. Curriculum planning cannot happen in isolation, particularly when the world of work is changing so quickly. By bringing employers and educators together, the College can better understand where the real skills gaps are emerging and how programmes, projects, placements and apprenticeships can respond. It also helps ensure that students are not only gaining subject knowledge, but also developing the wider behaviours that employers continue to place at the top of the list.
The discussion also highlighted an important point for businesses. Preparing for Generation Alpha is not just about asking young people to fit into existing workplaces. It is also about workplaces being ready to welcome, guide and learn from them. Existing staff have a vital role to play in mentoring new entrants, modelling professional standards and helping them turn feedback into progress. In return, younger employees can bring fresh ideas, different perspectives and new confidence in the tools and technologies that are reshaping modern industry.
Newbury College is inviting employers to help shape its careers, not courses curriculum and play an active role in developing the future workforce. By working in partnership with the College, businesses can share their expertise, influence training and help create opportunities to transform lives, while supporting students and apprentices to build the skills, confidence and behaviours needed for success. Find out more on the employers section of the Newbury College website at https://newbury-college.ac.uk/employers

Passion and perspective drive creative expression at Newbury College art show
Newbury College Art and Design students have celebrated creativity, skill and achievement at their annual End of Year Show.
The exhibition brought together final projects by students studying Art and Design at Levels 2, 3 and 4. Visitors experienced a diverse collection of visual art and thought-provoking design, created through a wide range of materials, techniques and creative approaches.
The show opened with a private view for friends and family on Monday 22 June. Students were joined by college governors, the Mayor of Newbury, Councillor Jo Day, and the Mayor’s Consort, Ian Jee. The exhibition then opened to the public from Tuesday 23 June to Thursday 25 June.
Level 2 and Level 3 students responded to the theme “PASSION! Exploring what drives creative expression”. Level 4 students continued to explore Perspective, the theme introduced for their mid-year exhibition in December 2025, with the work on show showcasing a culmination of their Final Major Project alongside brief themes such as Urban Legends.
Students were asked to choose a subject of special interest and communicate it through their final project. The open briefs encouraged them to develop a personal creative response while showing the research, experimentation and technical skills they had gained throughout the year.
The Level 2 programme introduces students to disciplines including drawing, painting, printmaking and digital design. It encourages experimentation, creative problem-solving and the development of ideas, leading to a personal final project.
At Level 3, students develop their creative practice through studio projects, contextual research and specialist technical work. They also build portfolios and gain experience of exhibitions, competitions, live briefs and industry collaboration.
The Level 4 Art, Design and Media Practice programme helps students bridge the gap between college and university or professional practice. Students explore disciplines including fine art, textiles, illustration, photography, printmaking, ceramics and design before specialising in an independent final project. The course also supports students to create professional portfolios, exhibit their work and prepare for careers in the creative industries.
The exhibition gave students valuable experience of presenting their work, discussing their creative decisions and engaging with an audience. These skills reflect Newbury College’s ‘Careers, not courses’ approach, which helps students prepare for higher education, employment, freelance work and other opportunities within the creative sector.
Level 4 student Emily Lewis said:
“I have really enjoyed my time on the Art and Design programme, and I feel it has really helped me and pushed me forward into pursuing my dream career. It inspired me to keep going and showed me that it is possible for me to achieve a job in the creative industries, and that it’s not just a silly dream.”
Fellow student Kara Bance said:
“This course has given me the confidence and support to experiment with new techniques and develop my ideas into meaningful pieces of art.”
The End of Year Show celebrated each student’s individual creative identity and the commitment behind their work. It also gave visitors the opportunity to discover emerging local talent and see the next generation of artists and designers developing their professional voices.
It is not too late to apply to study Art and Design at Newbury College this September. Whether you want to explore your creativity, develop specialist skills or prepare for university and a career in the creative industries, find out more and apply at newbury-college.ac.uk/art

Unlock your creativity and take your first step into the world of music production with the Level 2 Certificate in Music Technology. This programme is perfect if you are passionate about music and eager to learn how to create, record, and produce your own tracks using industry-standard software and equipment. Whether you dream of becoming a music producer, sound engineer, or DJ, this course provides the foundational skills to turn your passion into a career or hobby.

Units covered may include the following:
Five GSCE passes at grade 3 (D) or above, preferably to include Maths and English, or an equivalent vocational qualification at merit grade, and Functional Skills Maths and English, preferably at Level 1.
Students who have not yet achieved a grade 4 in GSCE Maths and English, study Functional Skills or GCSE Maths and English as part of their course.
This programme is designed for beginners, so no prior experience in music technology is necessary. However, a love for music and a keen interest in technology will be valuable. Basic computer skills are also recommended as you will be working with various software and digital tools. You need to be able to follow instructions, work as part of a team and be prepared to complete work outside of normal course hours, some of which will be in the evening.

You could move on to the Level 3 course in Music Technology, or even consider internships and entry-level roles in music production, live sound, or broadcasting. Whether you want to start a career in the music industry or just produce music for yourself, this certificate will set you on the right path.
Your progress will be assessed through practical assignments, which might include producing tracks, recording live performances, or presenting your own mixes.
Assignments set have an agreed hand-in date that needs to be met in order to meet the awarding body guidelines. Some units may also include externally marked assessment material.

You may have the chance to participate in work experience where you can gain hands-on experience. You will also engage with inspiring speakers from the industry who will share insights about their roles and career paths. College partnership with Educafe builds confidence and career skills
A partnership between Newbury College and Educafe is helping young people gain valuable workplace experience while supporting the local community.
The collaboration has created structured placements where students can build confidence, develop practical skills and learn how a community organisation operates which was featured by Educafe in their article Strengthening Youth Opportunities through Our Collaboration with Newbury College | Educafe.
Harrison Raithby joined Educafe to complete his Media Broadcast & Production T Level Industry Placement. He initially supported social media campaigns, website blogs and marketing activity.
As his placement developed, Harrison became involved in other areas of the organisation. He worked alongside staff and volunteers, supported the weekly community café and engaged with visitors from a range of backgrounds.
During the final months of his placement, Harrison took on a more community-facing role. He welcomed visitors, offered conversation and companionship, and helped create an inclusive atmosphere.
He also supported visitors with digital skills and language activities. This helped him strengthen his communication, teamwork and problem-solving skills.
Harrison took part in volunteer safeguarding training and attended volunteer appreciation events. He also received podcast development training, which expanded his creative and technical knowledge.
Subia Azmat from Educafe said: “I am incredibly proud of the progress he has made, both personally and professionally. I wish him the very best for his future.”
Educafe reported that Harrison had grown in confidence, initiative and independence throughout the placement. His willingness to learn allowed him to move from a mainly media-based role into the organisation’s busy operations team.
The partnership supports Newbury College’s ‘Careers, not courses’ approach by giving students practical experience in the workplace. Industry placements also benefit employers by bringing fresh ideas into their organisation, helping to develop future talent and giving them the chance to shape the skills needed in their sector.
Newbury College and Educafe hope to continue developing the partnership so that more young people can access meaningful work experience and contribute to their community.
Employers interested in offering work experience opportunities to Newbury College students can visit newbury-college.ac.uk/employers to find out more.

Creative Media, Production and Technology Level 3
Get started on your journey to a career in the media industry. This dynamic and engaging programme enables you to develop you passion for media to explore, develop and refine your creative abilities within a structured and supportive learning environment. You will build a strong portfolio of practical work to support progression into a wide range of higher education pathways. Many students go on to advance their studies through the Top Up year - Level 3 Extended Diploma in Creative Media Production and Technology, further strengthening their creative and technical expertise.
Develop the critical, creative, and practical skills needed for success in art, design, and related creative industries. Throughout this programme you will build an informed awareness of different artistic perspectives and approaches, learning how to research, analyse and evaluate information to generate innovative ideas and creative solutions.
You will be supported to develop confidence in using a range of practical and technical methods safely and effectively, applying these skills to solve complex creative challenges. You will also refine your ability to review and evaluate your own work, taking responsibility for learning, decision-making, and personal development.
The development of strong organisational skills, including research, planning and time management, will enable you to pursue progression opportunities with independence. You will also practice and enhance your ability to present yourself and your creative outcomes professionally to a variety of audiences.
Minimum of four GCSEs at grade 4 (C) or above, including English and Maths.
You'll have an interest in exploring and developing original ideas, along with basic media and technical skills such as capturing and editing media content. Good organisation and time-management skills are also essential, as students often plan recordings, manage workflows, and work independently outside class time. Above all, motivated learners who are eager to experiment, develop their creative practice, and build a professional portfolio will thrive on this programme.
UAL Diploma in Creative Media Production & Technology Level 3
Following the achievement of this programme you'll have the opportunity to study the Top-Up Extended Diploma and progress to degree level courses, employment in media production, film, television or other creative subjects.
Assessment is entirely coursework-based and focuses on practical, creative project work. Learners are assessed through a mixture of observations, short tests, written tasks and project-based assignments, all designed to mirror real industry practices.
Because the course is heavily project-based, students are often required to work independently outside of class time to develop ideas, plan productions, carry out research, and complete practical tasks.
As part of the wider study programme,you will have the opportunity to take part in work experience to help you develop real-world skills and gain insight into the creative media industry.

Careers, Not Courses
At Newbury College, we are focused on supporting your future career development, which is embedded in our Careers, not Courses ethos. So whether you looking to start a career in a subject you love or looking to take your current career to the next level look no further than Newbury College and University Centre Newbury!
Our high-quality vocational training programmes are tailored to support your learning and career development at every stage of your journey.
Book a meeting to discuss your options or use our Programme Picker to find the perfect path for you.
Discover the next-level qualifications that combine class work with real work.
Build the future with Apprenticeships.
Engaging workshops to engage pupils and support their career aspirations.
Discover how we engage with employers to provide industry experience and progression opportunities.
Train the next generation as a teacher.
We work closely with top employers to develop a career-based curriculum that gives you the skills and qualifications you need to succeed in your chosen field. Through creating a fully immersive learning environment, we combine hands-on technical training with real-world work experience, giving you the tools to excel in the workplace of tomorrow.
What does "Careers, not courses" mean?
If you are looking to start or develop a particular career path then vocational education could be better for your progression than traditional A Levels or university courses. Our programmes are designed to target the requirements of industry and the aspirations of you as an individual.
Vocational study programmes have different assessment methods to purely academic studies, engaging a wide range of methods to deliver and assess your skills.
We involve our business partners in many aspects of our curriculum planning and delivery. This ensures that our programmes meet the needs of employers and job sectors, increasing your employability and opportunities.
Our programmes take advantage of industry-appropriate technology, like Microsoft Office 365, to enhance on-site sessions with online learning and support. Our digital platforms enable you to access learning and resources from home and the workplace, in addition to benefiting from the face-to-face interaction with their tutors and peers.
So whether you're just starting out on your career path or looking to take your skills to the next level, Newbury College and University Centre Newbury have everything you need to succeed. Join us today and start building the career of your dreams!

Transform your creativity into a career.
Art and Design covers a broad spectrum of skills in solving problems, communicating ideas, and shaping the world around us. By studying Art and Design, you’ll learn to think differently, push boundaries, and discover the power of your unique vision.
In our comprehensive programmes, you’ll explore a wide range of techniques and mediums, from traditional drawing and painting to digital design and mixed media. You’ll develop critical skills in visual communication, concept development, and creative problem-solving while working with industry-standard tools and software. Guided by experienced artists and designers, you’ll experiment with different forms of expression, hone your craft, and create a professional portfolio that showcases your talent and originality.
Beyond the classroom, you can collaborate on real-world projects, participate in exhibitions, and connect with creative professionals through guest lectures and work placements. Whether you’re interested in graphic design, illustration, fine art, or 3D modelling, our programmes equip you with the knowledge and experience to pursue a dynamic career in the creative industries or further your studies at leading art institutions.

Beauty and Hairdressing
Turn your passion into a profession.
The Beauty Therapy and Hairdressing industries are about boosting confidence, expressing creativity, and staying ahead of the latest trends and techniques. By studying Beauty Therapy and Hairdressing, you will gain the expertise and practical experience needed to excel in these fast-paced, ever-evolving industries.
Our hands-on programmes cover a wide range of skills, from cutting, colouring, and styling hair to mastering beauty treatments such as skincare, makeup, and nail artistry. You will learn from experienced professionals in our industry-standard salons and treatment rooms, ensuring you develop both the technical skills and customer service expertise essential to success. We focus on providing real-world training, with opportunities to practice on clients and perfect your craft using top-quality products and equipment.
You’ll also benefit from work placements, which will give you a taste of the industry and help you build a network of contacts. Whether your ambition is to work in a high-end salon, start your own beauty business, or pursue specialist roles in areas like spa therapy or fashion styling, our programmes prepare you for a rewarding and creative career in Beauty Therapy and Hairdressing.

Child Care and Education
Shape minds and make a lasting impact.
If you’re passionate about helping people learn, grow, and thrive, our Child Care (Early Years) and Education programmes offer you the skills and knowledge to make a real difference.
Our comprehensive courses cover essential areas, from child development and safeguarding to creating engaging and inclusive learning environments. You will learn how to observe, support, and nurture physical, emotional, and intellectual growth through interactive activities, play, and structured learning. Led by experienced educators, you will develop skills in communication, planning, and behaviour management, preparing you to build strong relationships with children, learners, families, and colleagues.
Beyond the classroom, you may have the chance to gain practical experience in local nurseries, schools, and early years settings, where you will apply your knowledge and skills in real-world situations. Whether your goal is to become an early years practitioner, teaching assistant, or move into specialised roles, our programmes provide you with the foundation to inspire and support the next generation.
